transcript.text: lg w/d keeps saying dE n wont start?? door is shut

Frustrating when the door's clearly shut and it still won't go. - The door isn't quite latching: a sock or bit of washing caught in the rubber seal can stop it clicking fully home.
• The catch (the little hook on the door) is worn or bent, or the door has dropped slightly on its hinge, so it doesn't push into the lock properly.
• The door interlock itself (the electrical lock behind the slot) has failed and isn't telling the machine the door is shut.
• Less often, a loose connection to the lock or a control board fault. 1. Reset it: switch off at the socket, unplug, and leave it 5 minutes. Plug back in and try again. If it starts, it was a one-off glitch.
2. Open the door, run your hand round the seal to make sure nothing is trapped, then close it firmly until you hear a clear click and press Start. If it works now, it simply wasn't latching.
3. With it unplugged, look at the hook on the door and the slot it goes into. Is the hook cracked, bent or loose, and does the door line up squarely when closed, or does it sag? A damaged hook or sagging door points to the catch or hinge rather than the lock.
4. Close the door, then press Start while gently pressing the door shut with your hand. If it only starts when pushed, it's an alignment or worn catch problem. If nothing changes and you never hear the lock click, the door interlock becomes the main suspect. Don't try to bypass the lock or force anything. If the hook and hinge look fine and it never clicks locked, the interlock is the most likely part. It's a fairly common replacement, but it does mean taking the front seal and panel area apart, so many people prefer an engineer for that bit. Let me know what happens with the click and the push test, as that's the main thing that separates the causes.
ok did the reset, still dE. theres a duvet in tho, its bulging against the glass n a corner is squashed in the seal. it closes but springs back a bit

That duvet is probably the culprit. dE on an LG means the machine can't confirm the door is closed and locked. A corner squashed in the seal, plus a drum packed so full the duvet pushes against the glass, stops the hook going far enough into the lock, which is why the door springs back a bit. The machine is doing exactly what it should by refusing to start. 1. Open the door and pull the trapped corner out of the seal. Push the whole duvet back so nothing sits in the rubber fold, including round the bottom where it's easy to miss.
2. If it's still bulging against the glass, the drum is too full. Check the duvet size suits your drum: a double or king duvet is often too bulky for a typical washer-dryer, especially one with a thick tog. Taking it out and refolding it loosely sometimes gives enough room. If it can't fit without pushing on the door, it really needs a bigger machine, such as a launderette.
3. Close the door firmly until you hear a clear click and it stays flush without springing back. Then press Start. If it locks and runs, that was the whole problem. One thing to expect: with one big item like a duvet, the machine may cut back or skip the spin because the load is unbalanced. That's normal behaviour, not a new fault. If the drum is empty or nothing is in the way, the door shuts cleanly and clicks, and it still shows dE, then the next suspects are the door catch or the door interlock. Let me know if that happens and we'll go from there. Don't force the door shut against the duvet or try to hold it closed while it runs.
ok pulled the duvet out n tried towels instead, starts fine. so its just the duvet being too big?

Yes, that's it. If it starts fine with towels and the door shuts cleanly, the lock and catch are working properly. The duvet was simply too bulky. Nothing needs replacing. To stop it happening again: if a duvet has to be squashed in to get the door shut, or it bulges against the glass, it's too big for the drum. A properly fitting duvet should leave a hand's width of space at the top of the drum. It also needs room to tumble so it actually gets clean and rinsed. For bigger or thicker duvets, a launderette's large machines are the easy answer. If dE ever comes back with a normal load and nothing caught in the seal, that's when the door catch or interlock would be worth looking at. Is there anything else I can help with?
